p:cNvPr.descr: A two-part diagram shows (a) the steps in the targeting of nuclear proteins and (b) a black-and-white microscopic image of the nuclear envelope. The diagram shows the process of targeting nuclear proteins. The setting of the process is the nuclear envelope, which divides the diagram into a light yellow top half, which is the cytosol, and a light blue bottom half, which is the nucleoplasm. The nuclear envelope consists of alternating units of membrane, which is represented by an oval lined with light yellow that is pale blue on the inside, representing the intermembrane space. To the left and right of these are the nuclear pores, which are openings lined completely with small blue proteins labeled "nuclear pore complex." Below the pore itself is a partial basket-shaped structure. This is the nuclear basket. There are a total of three nuclear pores in the diagram, interspersed with sections of membrane. The process begins at the top with the input of a nuclear protein, which is a very small pale blue coiled structure with a red residue near the bottom end. It is labeled NLS. It is shown being added to the cycle with a convergent arrow. This step is labeled (1) on the left. The arrow curves left to show the nuclear protein bound to an alpha-beta importin complex, which consists of a slightly flattened, green protein labeled "beta", with a flat, cushion like light green protein on its top, labeled "alpha." The nuclear protein bonds to the curve in the alpha protein right at the NLS. From here there is an arrow pointing down and left, then the same image again, showing the complex moving down toward the nuclear envelope. Below this is another arrow pointing down, labeled (2) on the left. The arrow points down through the nuclear pore, which has wavy blue residues reaching up from its edges. These are cytosolic fibrils. On the inside of the nucleus, on the other side of the nuclear pore, is the same complex with the alpha and beta importin attached up to the nuclear protein. From here, there is an arrow which splits in two. The top arrow is labeled (3) and points to a complex that consists of the beta transportin attached up to a mint green spherical protein labeled Ran-GTP. From here, the arrow curves right and upward, back up and out through another nuclear pore. This arrow is labeled (5) on the left. The arrow points up to an empty beta importin, from which there is an arrow curving left back to step 1. Returning back down to step 3, after the nuclear protein has entered the nucleus, there is an arrow that curves more downward and to the right. It points to the nuclear protein attached only to the alpha importin. To the right of this is another arrow labeled (4). It has a divergent arrow showing detachment of the nuclear protein. The arrow points right to a complex consisting of the Ran-GTP, sitting on the alpha importin, which sits on top of a rounded light red rectangular importin labeled CAS. From here, an arrow curves upward to exit the nuclear membrane via a nuclear pore. It points to the same lone beta importin described earlier. Above the lone beta importin is a lone alpha importin. It has two arrows above it, both curving up and to the right. The right arrow has a divergent arrow on the right showing removal of CAS. The two arrows point right to the Ran-GDP. From the Ran-GDP, an arrow curves down with a convergent arrow on the right which shows addition of NTF2, which is pale blue and is rectangular with a semicircular cutout at the bottom. The arrow points down to step (6), which shows the Ran-GDP fitted into the cutout below NTF2. Below this is another arrow, which points down through the rightmost nuclear pore, down to the NTF2-Ran-GDP complex again. From here, there is an arrow pointing down. It is labeled (7) on the left. Also on the left is a convergent-divergent arrow showing addition of GTP and removal of NTF2. On the right is a divergent arrow showing removal of GDP, facilitated by Ran-GEF, which is represented by a purple oval. The arrow points down to the lone Ran-GTP. From this point, there are two arrows. One arrow curves left to point to the Ran-GTP-alpha-CAS complex previously described. The other points down and curves left to follow the bottom of the diagram, only to curve upward and point to the Ran-GTP attached to the beta importin at step 3. (b) A black-and-white micrograph of the nuclear envelope. It is dark gray and granular, and has several small cutouts in it which are partially covered. These are the nuclear pores.
